draft.title: Designing a Hypothetical Prompt Regression Test Suite for Local LLMs
draft.body: I'm exploring a structured approach for prompt regression testing in local LLM development. The goal is to create a consistent evaluation method. This is a hypothetical experiment design, and no actual results are available. The plan involves using a fixed set of 12 test prompts (F1) that include both questions with clear answers and scenarios where information is insufficient (F3). The core of the testing would be to compare an older prompt version against a newer one using the exact same model settings and parameters on identical hardware (F2). This controlled comparison aims to isolate the effect of prompt modifications. It's crucial to reiterate that this is a conceptual framework, and no performance improvements have been measured or are currently available (F4). I'm seeking community input on this testing methodology before any implementation. What are your thoughts on this structure for evaluating prompt changes?
draft.plan: Introduce the hypothetical prompt regression test design. Detail the use of a fixed prompt set and controlled comparisons. Explicitly state the absence of results. Invite discussion on the methodology.

draft.title: Hypothetical Prompt Regression Testing: Design Considerations
draft.body: This post outlines a hypothetical framework for designing a prompt regression test suite for local LLMs. The objective is to establish a repeatable method for evaluating prompt efficacy without relying on pre-existing results. We propose using a fixed set of 12 test prompts, covering both directly answerable questions and cases where information is insufficient. The core idea is to compare the output of an old prompt against a new variant using identical model settings and parameters on the same hardware. This controlled comparison is crucial for isolating the impact of prompt changes. It's important to note that this is a conceptual design, and no actual performance improvements or measurements have been conducted or are available at this stage. The goal is to solicit feedback on the proposed testing methodology itself, before any implementation or data collection occurs. What are your thoughts on structuring such a test?
